entities.summary:
Iufni was an ancient Egyptian pharaoh of the 13th Dynasty during the Second Intermediate Period.

Born in unknown circumstances, Iufni ascended to the throne around 1850 BCE and ruled for approximately 50 years, leaving behind a legacy that would shape the course of Egyptian history.

One of his most significant achievements was the unification of Upper and Lower Egypt, which he accomplished through strategic alliances and military campaigns. This feat not only restored stability but also paved the way for a golden age of art, architecture, and culture during the New Kingdom period.

Despite his many accomplishments, Iufni's reign was marked by turmoil and conflict, including a series of devastating wars with neighboring kingdoms.

His death in 1800 BCE at the hands of a rival faction would ultimately lead to the downfall of the 13th Dynasty and the rise of the Hyksos, a Semitic people who would go on to shape Egyptian history for centuries to come.

Iufni's legacy is still remembered today through various artifacts and inscriptions found throughout ancient Egypt, including the famous 'Stele of Iufni' which details his military campaigns and administrative achievements.
